messages:
maya: FYI - we need to align OTel/Prom labels for routing/quota telemetry. runtime + infra inputs required. proposing a short convention so dashboards don't explode.

sam: what specific metrics are in-scope? routing decisions, per-route latency, quota usage?

liam: agree keep it tight. main worry = high-cardinality labels (route_name, user_id, model_variant). need gating.

zoe: rough naming draft:
```
# Prom metric name (snake_case)
redwood_runtime_request_count_total{service,env,route_id,model_variant}
redwood_runtime_request_latency_ms_bucket{service,env,route_id}
redwood_infra_gpu_util_percent{region,instance_type}
```
Use OTel resource attributes for deployment/region, avoid user_id on Prom metrics.

emily: rollout UX + dashboards: product wants per-route success-rate and canary split visible in console. can we expose aggregated route labels for that?

maya: proposal: keep Prom labels to low-cardinality keys only: service, env, route_id (hashed, optional), model_class (small set), quantized_flag. Use OTel spans/attributes for high-cardinality trace-level fields. Cardinality gate: route_name allowed only on debug builds / sample 0.01.

sam: +1 to hashed route_id. for model_variant we can allow 'base', 'quant', 'int8' values only. please add examples to docs.

liam: small nit - prefer prefix 'redwood_' for owned metrics and 'redwood_runtime_' for runtime-specific. Also recommend label naming: 'env' -> 'deployment_env' to avoid colliding.

zoe: I'll draft a README with schema + dashboard mapping + example Grafana queries. can we sync tomorrow 10am? @sam @liam :thumbsup: 

maya: SGTM. I'll create a one-pager and a tiny RFC for the gating rules. Owners: eng-runtime (liam), eng-platform (maya/zoe). Thanks all :raised_hands:
